title: Diokno objects to qualifying Dela Fuente as expert witness on money laundering
summary: House prosecutor and Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno on Thursday objected to the defense"s presentation of witness AML Consulting PH head Rainer dela Fuente, saying that Vice President Sara Duterte was not…

blocks.text: House prosecutor and Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno on Thursday objected to the defense’s presentation of witness AML Consulting PH head Rainer dela Fuente, saying that Vice President Sara Duterte was not facing any charges of money laundering.
While defense counsel Mark Vinluan presented Dela Fuente’s credentials, Diokno questioned the relevance of the witness to the impeachment charges against the Vice President.

“The witness is apparently delivering his credentials on anti-money laundering but the respondent in this case is not being charged with money laundering crimes. The issue before this court are all centered on unexplained wealth, non-declaration of SALN, and participation in business. And I haven’t heard anything from this witness that would qualify him on those matters,” Diokno said.

However, Vinluan maintained that there were allegations of money laundering under one of the impeachment articles. There was a brief, tense moment between Vinluan and Diokno, where the two spoke over each other.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero intervened, letting Vinluan speak first.

“They presented an AMLC witness, and they made interpretations on the data as well. They also presented their own witness, your honor. It is our position, your honor, that we also have the prerogative to present our own expert on the matter,” Vinluan said.
Diokno disagreed with Vinluan, saying that money laundering was too serious of a charge to allow it to pass.

Later on, Vinluan presented a portion from the articles of impeachment, which read: “Relevantly, the Investigation Reports from the AMLC on respondent and her spouse indicate that the bank transactions involving their bank accounts may have been involved in predicate offenses of money laundering, particularly: (a) drug trafficking and related offenses; (b) graft and corrupt practices; and (c) malversation of public funds.”
While initially allowing the defense to continue its questioning, Escudero would later agree with Diokno, issuing a clarification.

“The chair has given you enough leeway on this aspect but I have to cite and state that the Honorable Diokno is correct. AMLC or violation of the AMLC is not per se, part of the charge in Article II. Although it is mentioned in pages 12 and 14 of the Articles of Impeachment as the chair stated earlier, it was merely cited as the basis or evidence of the supposed unexplained or ill-gotten wealth. But there is no specific charge. Neither is there any issue that this court will rule upon regarding any purported violation of the Anti-Money Laundering law,” Escudero said. —AOL, GMA News
